Operator:
Good day, and welcome to the ShopSphere Inc. Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question and answer session. Instructions for joining the question and answer session will be given at that time. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, operator. Good afternoon, everyone, and welcome to ShopSphere Inc.'s Q3 2024 earnings call. Joining me today are Jordan Lee, CEO; Sarah Chen, CFO; Mike Patel, COO; Lisa Wong, CMO; and Raj Singh, CTO.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that this call may contain forward-looking statements, including our expectations for future financial performance, business strategies, and market trends. These statements are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete list of these risks and uncertainties.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Jordan Lee, CEO of ShopSphere Inc.

Jordan Lee:
Thank you, Alex, and good afternoon, everyone. We are pleased to report a strong Q3 performance, driven by robust GMV expansion and the early momentum from our international scaling efforts. We saw significant growth in key metrics, with GMV surging 28% year-over-year to $18.7 billion, well ahead of our guidance, alongside active customer growth and improved repeat purchase rates.

Our focus remains on operational leverage and marketplace monetization. We are also excited about the initial traction we are seeing with our holiday season ramp-up, where we've strategically built inventory levels to capture expected demand surges across categories like electronics and apparel.

We are investing heavily in supply chain resilience to counter logistics disruptions.

We are focused on improving fulfillment efficiencies and cost per order.

Finally, we are committed to accelerating our global footprint, with international markets now representing a larger share of our growth.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Sarah Chen, our CFO, to discuss our financial results in more detail.

Sarah Chen:
Thank you, Jordan. Good afternoon, everyone. This is Sarah Chen taking over for the financial highlights. Today, I'll focus on our standout Q3 results, starting with net income and earnings per share, where we delivered figures that meaningfully exceeded expectations, underscoring the strength of our core e-commerce engine and the early payoffs from our operational leverage initiatives.

Starting with the headline numbers: We reported net income of $285 million, up 32% year-over-year and well ahead of our guidance midpoint of $240 million and the Street's consensus of $252 million. This translated to diluted EPS of $1.78, a 35% increase from last year and beating expectations by 12%, with consensus at $1.59. Adjusted for one-time items—like the $15 million gain from our divestiture of a non-core legacy logistics subsidiary—our non-GAAP net income came in at $270 million, or $1.68 per share, still surpassing guidance by 8%.

What drove this outperformance? Top-line momentum was robust, with total net revenue hitting $8.7 billion, up 22% YoY, fueled by 18% GMV growth to $12.5 billion—though our full GMV picture is even stronger at $18.7 billion when factoring in marketplace acceleration. Our active customer base expanded 14% to 185 million globally, with repeat purchase rates climbing to 68%, a 300 basis point improvement, thanks to our AI-powered recommendation engine, which now powers 75% of sessions and lifted conversion rates by 220 basis points to 4.2%. Average order value rose 3% to $52, driven by cross-sell success in high-margin categories like electronics and beauty, where we outperformed Amazon in share gains per SimilarWeb data.

On the bottom line, gross margin expanded 180 basis points to 42.1%, our strongest in three quarters. This was propelled by a higher mix of our private-label ShopSphere Essentials lineup, which grew 45% YoY and now accounts for 22% of units sold, delivering 55% gross margins versus 38% on third-party marketplace items. We also realized $120 million in supply chain savings from our NextGen Fulfillment network—think advanced robotic sortation centers—which reduced fulfillment costs per unit by 11% despite 25% volume growth. Operating expenses scaled efficiently: Marketing spend as a percentage of revenue dipped to 14.2% from 15.8%, reflecting a 22% drop in CAC to $28 per new customer via refined Facebook and TikTok attribution models and our first-party data loop from the ShopSphere app.

Regionally, North America remains our powerhouse, contributing 62% of net revenue with $5.4 billion, up 25% YoY, and EPS contribution of $1.12—beating local expectations amid strong back-to-school demand and same-day delivery penetration hitting 45% in top metros. APAC accelerated to 28% revenue growth at $2.4 billion, led by India and Southeast Asia, where our hyperlocal quick-commerce arm—competing head-on with Flipkart and Shopee—doubled GMV to $1.8 billion on urban grocery penetration. Europe, at 10% of revenue, grew a more modest 12% to $900 million but saw margin compression to 39% due to VAT headwinds and the DMA's gatekeeper rules; that said, our EPS impact there was still positive at $0.22, bolstered by localized assortment in fashion via partnerships akin to Zalando's model.

Strategically, these results validate our Flywheel 2.0 playbook: investing $450 million this year in seller tools to boost our marketplace take rate to 18.5%—up from 16.2%—while accelerating Prime-like subscription adoption, now at 65 million members globally, driving 52% of revenue. We're also leaning into adjacent verticals; our fresh grocery initiative, launched in 12 U.S. markets, achieved breakeven in Q3 with 30% AOV uplift, positioning us against Instacart and Amazon Fresh. Forward-looking, we see sustained tailwinds from macroeconomic stabilization—U.S. consumer spending on discretionary e-comm up 8% per Census Bureau data—and our $2 billion share repurchase authorization signals confidence in 15-20% EPS growth through FY25.

Of course, risks remain: currency volatility shaved 50 basis points off EPS, and we're monitoring tariff escalations in apparel from Asia. But with free cash flow at a record $1.2 billion—up 40%—we're well-capitalized for M&A, like our recent $300 million tuck-in of a Latin Am quick-commerce player.

Building on these profitability drivers, let's dive deeper into fulfillment cost per order, or FCPO, a key operational metric encompassing costs from order picking and packing in our fulfillment centers, to outbound shipping, inbound freight, and returns processing. It's critical for gross margins in this competitive landscape, where peers like Amazon and Shopify players face similar pressures.

In Q3 2024, FCPO came in at $7.12, a 16% year-over-year decline from $8.47 in Q3 2023, and sequentially down 4% from $7.42 in Q2 2024. This marks our 10th straight quarter of improvement, with a trailing 12-month average of $7.38—below the industry benchmark of $9.50 for mid-tier online retailers like Wayfair and Etsy. As a percentage of revenue, FCPO now represents 12.8%, down from 15.9% a year ago, contributing 210 basis points to gross margin expansion to 42.1%.

Over the past few years, during the 2021 pandemic surge, FCPO spiked to $9.82 due to labor shortages and expedited rates; post-2022, we've achieved a compound annual decline of 18%. The progression shows: Q3 2022 at $9.15, up 12% from peak inflation and fuel costs; Q3 2023 at $8.47, down 8% from initial automation; Q2 2024 at $7.42, down 14% from network densification; Q3 2024 at $7.12, down 16% thanks to AI and machine learning optimizations. This outperforms Amazon's 8-10% YoY improvements.

Breaking down components: Pick-and-pack, 45% of FCPO, down 22% YoY to $3.21 per order, thanks to over 1,200 autonomous guided vehicles across top U.S. centers, modeled after Ocado but customized for our SKU mix—AGV utilization at 92%, reducing labor hours by 28%, plus AI dynamic slotting cutting picker travel by 35% via GreyOrange partnership. Outbound shipping, 35%, improved 14% to $2.49, with volume discounts from UPS and FedEx, route optimization shifting 24% to ground, saving $0.18 per package. Inbound and returns, 20%, down 12% to $1.42, via vendor-managed inventory reducing inbound by 19% and AI returns prediction flagging 68% pre-shipment.

Regionally: North America at $7.05 with 28 centers including micro-fulfillment in urban areas for 85% next-day; Europe at $8.24, improved 15% YoY despite VAT and Brexit via DHL partnerships; APAC best at $5.91 via SF Express, countering tariffs with Vietnam nearshoring.

We're targeting sub-$6.50 by 2025 with $450 million capex in robotics and edge-computing, plus sustainability like reusable totes saving $0.09 per order and boosting NPS. Q4 FCPO guide $7.00-$7.20, with hedged carrier contracts.

Transitioning to logistics and shipping costs, which faced headwinds from supply chain disruptions but where we've taken proactive steps. Total logistics costs hit $285 million, up 28% YoY from $222 million, or 14.7% of revenue—up 240 basis points YoY. Last-mile, 55% of spend, up 35%; inbound up 22%. This exceeds some peers but reflects our volume growth.

Drivers included transpacific freight rates up 320% to $5,200 per FEU from Red Sea attacks adding 10-14 days and $1,500-$2,000 costs; U.S. port congestion delaying 15% of containers, costing $12 million. North America up 32% from labor and diesel; Europe 24% from strikes; APAC 18% milder via localized sourcing, though typhoons hit.

Mitigations: AI dynamic routing with Flexport saving $18 million, targeting 20%; new Mexico MFCs cutting transit to 7 days; in-sourced urban fleets trimming 15%; safety stock at 45 days with VMI; dynamic surcharges recovering 40% costs.

Q4 moderation to 14.2%, full-year $1.15-$1.18 billion, with margins to 42.5%.

On GMV growth, we hit $18.7 billion, 28% YoY from $14.6 billion and 10.2% QoQ from $17.0 billion, beating 24-27% YoY and 7-9% QoQ guidance by 150 basis points YoY. Outpacing industry 15-18%.

YoY drivers: Buyers up 22% to 145 million, adding 12 million mostly emerging; AOV +5% to $172 on electronics +35%, beauty +28%; take rate +80 bps to 19.2% via BNPL at 45% and logistics 62%. North America 26% to $9.7 billion; APAC 42% to $5.8 billion, India +55%; Europe 18% to $2.4 billion.

QoQ: AI personalization +12% conversions, repeats to 68%; logistics under 24 hours; quick commerce +45% to $1.2 billion.

Q4 guide 26-29% YoY, 11-13% QoQ.

As we eye holidays, inventory at $2.8 billion, +18% YoY: Electronics $896 million +22%, apparel $700 million +15%, home/beauty $784 million +20%, other $420 million +10%. DIO 62 days vs. 72 industry, safety at 95th percentile.

Q4 GMV $12.5-13.2 billion, 22-28% YoY; NA $8.1-8.6 billion +25%, EMEA +18%, APAC/LATAM +30%. Powered by AI forecasting error to 8%, WMS dynamic slotting -22% pick time, eco-inventory.

Finally, international expansion: 28% of GMV at $2.8 billion, +52% YoY, +18% QoQ, outpacing U.S. Europe $1.18 billion + YoY buyers to 14.2 million, repeats 62%, London DC 95% OTD. APAC $870 million +78%, India $450 million +105%, Indonesia +140%. LATAM $504 million +41%, Mexico $220 million. MEA $252 million +112%. Powered by Shopify Plus, OMS, ML demand prediction. Targeting $12 billion annualized by FY25.

Our Q3 revenue was $10.2 billion, up 25% YoY. Gross margin 42.1%. OpEx $4.1 billion, 40% of revenue. Marketing optimized. Net income reaffirmed strong. Cash $3.5 billion. Full-year guidance: revenue $38-40 billion, EPS $6.50-$7.00.

Now I'll turn it over to Mike Patel to discuss operations.

Mike Patel:
Thanks, Sarah. Operationally, we focused on network densification and AI optimizations. Shipping times improved by 20%. Fulfillment costs down 16% per order as detailed. We're implementing new robotic systems across DCs.

Now I'll turn it over to Lisa Wong.

Lisa Wong:
Thanks, Mike. From marketing, strong results from TikTok integrations and Meta campaigns. CAC $28, down 22%. Brand awareness up 25%. Focusing on first-party data and personalization.

Now I'll turn it over to Raj Singh.

Raj Singh:
Thanks, Lisa. Tech-wise, focused on AI recommendations and OMS upgrades. Website uptime 99.99%. Mobile app usage up 30%. Investing in edge computing and personalization v2.0.

Operator, we are now ready for questions.

Operator:
Instructions for the question and answer session. Our first question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs.

John Smith:
Thanks, and congrats on the quarter. On the EPS beat to $1.78, can you expand on sustainability and any guide changes?

Jordan Lee:
Thanks, John. As Sarah outlined, the beat came from GMV strength, margin expansion via private labels, and efficiency gains. We're reaffirming full-year but see upside from holidays and international.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Emily Chen with Morgan Stanley.

Emily Chen:
Great results. On fulfillment costs at $7.12, what gives confidence in continued declines amid volumes?

Sarah Chen:
Emily, our 10-quarter streak reflects automation like AGVs at 92% utilization, AI slotting, and regional optimizations. Q4 guide holds with capex ramp.

Operator:
Our next question comes from David Lee with JPMorgan.

David Lee:
Impressive resilience on logistics disruptions—Red Sea, ports. How are you hedging for Q4 peaks?

Mike Patel:
David, AI routing saved $18 million already, Mexico MFCs cut exposure, and VMI/dynamic surcharges protect. Expect moderation as rates normalize.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Sarah Kim with Barclays.

Sarah Kim:
TikTok and personalization drove buyers—any shift in marketing mix for holidays?

Lisa Wong:
Sarah, yes, 60% to performance channels like TikTok Shop at 3.2% conversions, ROAS strong. Holiday focus on Gen Z bundling.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Mike Johnson with Citi.

Mike Johnson:
International at 52% growth—any bottlenecks in APAC/LATAM scaling?

Raj Singh:
Mike, our OMS handles 150 carriers, ML cuts stockouts 37%. New DCs and local payments like UPI keep momentum; FY25 target solid.

Operator:
There are no further questions at this time. I would now like to turn the call back over to Jordan Lee for closing remarks.

Jordan Lee:
Thank you for joining us today. We are confident in our ability to continue to execute our strategy and deliver long-term value for our shareholders. We look forward to speaking with you again next quarter.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
